_about: Flow Wolf: Theurge — the class, its features, the Set of the Current options and the eleven Shapes. Mechanics carried over from the SW5E Consular (full Flow caster, d6); every line of text is Bad Eden's own. Archetypes (the Ways) live in theurge-ways-*.json. Built by tools/build-packs.mjs.

classes.name: Flow Wolf: Theurge

choices.title: One with the Flow
choices.hint: Which score rises by 4 (and its maximum by 4): Wisdom or Charisma.

classes.description:
A woman in a patched duster stands in a dry creek bed while a raider truck comes down on her at forty miles an hour. She lifts one hand, and the creek remembers being water. The truck hydroplanes on nothing and folds itself around a cottonwood.

On the water tower at dusk a boy sits with his eyes shut and feels every heartbeat in the town below him: the slow ones, the frightened ones, the one three streets over that is burning up with fever. He breathes out. The fever breaks.

A man in a good coat talks quietly with the sheriff on the courthouse steps. Her hand drifts off her holster. The deputies will swear afterward that she just agreed with him, that's all. Something behind the man's smile is very old and has not eaten in a long time.

Theurges are the Flow Wolves who cast. The Flow runs through everything that survived the Shattering, and through a few things that didn't, and a Theurge has learned to put both hands in it: to mend and to scorch, to lift a truck or a mood, and, for the strongest of them, to catch a glimpse of what is coming downstream.

Hands in the Current

Wardens carry the arc-blade and Vigilants carry the grudge. A Theurge carries the knowing. They give their years to the mysteries of the Flow, where it pools, where it runs fast, what it wants, and that study lets them push a power further than anyone else can and bend it into shapes nobody taught them.

Upstream and Downstream

The Flow has a direction. Theurges who follow it upstream, toward the Sephirot and the source, spend what they have keeping towns standing and people breathing; folks call them wells. Theurges who let it carry them downstream, toward the Qliphoth and the pit, take what they want and call it the tide; folks call them sinks, though not to their faces. Plenty stand midstream and study the water, wanting no part of either bank.

Making a Theurge

When you make a Theurge, decide what the Flow is to you. A faith? A tool? A thing that happened to you? Did a Flow Wolf lodge find you young, or did you find the current alone in a bad year with nobody to tell you what it was? How does your town treat you now that they know, and how do you treat them? Do you see the Flow as upstream and downstream, or as one grey river that doesn't care which way you swim?

Quick Build

Make Wisdom or Charisma your highest ability score, then Dexterity. Pick the Hermit or Sage background.

Class Features

As a Theurge, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d6 per Theurge level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 6 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per Theurge level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor: None
Weapons: Simple weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma
Skills: Choose two from Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a quarterstaff or (b) any simple weapon
  • (a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
  • A coat with deep pockets, and a token from the lodge that found you (or didn't)

The Ways

At 3rd level you choose a Way, the lodge's word for the discipline a Theurge gives their life to. Your Way grants you features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.

features.name: Flowcasting
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 1st level

The Flow runs through everything that survived the Shattering, and through a few things that didn't. You've learned to put your hands in it. The powers you know are fragments of that knowing: habits of attention the current answers to.

Powers Known

You know four powers of your choice at 1st level, and you learn more as you gain levels, as shown in the Powers Known column of the Theurge table. You can't learn a power whose level is higher than your Max Power Level. Whenever you gain a Theurge level, you can also swap one power you know for another you qualify for.

Flow Points

You have a pool of Flow points equal to four times your Theurge level, plus your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice). You spend them to cast powers: a power costs its level plus one (at-will powers are free). You regain all spent Flow points when you finish a long rest.

Max Power Level

Most powers can be cast above their own level for a bigger effect, at one extra Flow point per level, up to your Max Power Level as shown on the Theurge table. Powers of 6th level and higher are heavy water: you can cast each of them once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

Casting Ability

Which ability you cast with depends on which way the power runs. Sephirotic powers use Wisdom. Qliphothic powers use Charisma. Unaligned powers use whichever of the two you prefer. Use that modifier whenever a power refers to your casting ability, when you set a saving throw DC for a power, and when you make an attack roll with one.

Power save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your casting ability modifier
Power attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your casting ability modifier

features.name: Draw Breath
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 1st level

You've learned to get some of it back by sitting still. When you finish a short rest, you can regain a number of Flow points equal to half your Theurge level (rounded down) plus your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Shaping
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 2nd level

The Flow isn't a spell list. It's a river, and you've learned where to put the rocks. When you cast a power, you can spend extra Flow points to change its shape. You know two Shapes at 2nd level, chosen from the list at the end of the class description, and you learn a third at 9th level and a fourth at 17th.

You can put only one Shape on a power when you cast it, unless the Shape says otherwise.

features.name: Flow Ward
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 2nd level

You can hold the current between yourself and a blow. When you're hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to pull the Flow up around you like a coat. Until the start of your next turn you have a bonus to AC equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1), and it counts against the attack that hit you.

You can use this feature twice. You gain one more use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level, and you regain all spent uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Upstream
features.description:
Set of the Current (Sephirotic), 3rd level

It runs toward the source through you, and it leaves something behind on the way. When you cast a Sephirotic power of 1st level or higher, you or one target of the power (your choice) gains an increase to both current and maximum hit points equal to the power's level. The increase lasts 1 minute.

Only one instance of this effect can be active at a time; a new one replaces the old.

features.name: Midstream
features.description:
Set of the Current (Unaligned), 3rd level

You stand in the middle and take it from both banks. Add both your Wisdom modifier and your Charisma modifier to your maximum Flow points, instead of just one.

features.name: Downstream
features.description:
Set of the Current (Qliphothic), 3rd level

It runs toward the pit through you, and it doesn't do anything by halves. When you roll damage for a Qliphothic power, treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2.

features.name: One with the Flow
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 20th level

There is no longer a line where you stop and the current starts. Your Wisdom or Charisma score increases by 4, and your maximum for that score increases by 4 (choose which when you reach 20th level).

You also have a signature: one 3rd-level power you know that costs you nothing to think. You can cast it at 3rd level without spending Flow points. Once you do, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. To cast it at a higher level, spend Flow points as normal.

features.name: One with the Flow: Wisdom
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 20th level

Your Wisdom score increases by 4, and your maximum for that score increases by 4.

features.name: One with the Flow: Charisma
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Theurge, 20th level

Your Charisma score increases by 4, and your maximum for that score increases by 4.

features.name: Careful Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power that forces creatures to make a saving throw, you can hold some of them out of the worst of it. Spend 1 extra Flow point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). Each chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the power.

features.name: Distant Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power with a range of 5 feet or more, you can spend 1 extra Flow point to double its range.

When you cast a power with a range of touch, you can spend 1 extra Flow point to give it a range of 30 feet instead.

features.name: Extended Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power with a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 extra Flow point to double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.

features.name: Heightened Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can spend 3 extra Flow points to give one target of the power disadvantage on its first saving throw against it.

features.name: Honed Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you roll damage for a power, you can spend 1 extra Flow point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.

You can use Honed Shape even if you've already put another Shape on the power.

features.name: Lingering Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power that requires concentration, you can spend 3 extra Flow points so that it doesn't let go when you do. If you lose concentration on the power, it doesn't end until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Pinpoint Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power that forces creatures in an area to make a saving throw, you can instead spend 1 Flow point and make a ranged power attack against one creature that would be in that area. On a hit, the target suffers the power's effects as if it had failed its saving throw, and nobody else is affected.

features.name: Quickened Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power with a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 extra Flow points to cast it as a bonus action instead.

features.name: Refocused Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you have to make a Constitution saving throw to keep concentration on a power, you can use your reaction and spend 2 Flow points to succeed automatically.

You can use Refocused Shape even if you've already put another Shape on the power.

features.name: Seeking Shape
features.description:
Shape

If you miss with a power that calls for an attack roll, you can spend 2 Flow points to reroll the attack. You must use the new roll.

You can use Seeking Shape even if you've already put another Shape on the power.

features.name: Twinned Shape
features.description:
Shape

When you cast a power that can target only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend extra Flow points equal to the power's level (1 for an at-will power) to choose a second target in range for the same power.
